newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - White metals seen strong, gold soggy.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - White metals seen strong, gold soggy.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Precious metals markets are likely to diversify on Tuesday, with strength in the white metals, notably the PGMs, but little excitement in gold, analysts said.
Short-covering in platinum and palladium has already lifted those markets in the Far East, against the ongoing background of a dearth of Russian supplies, they noted.
PLATINUM/PALLADIUM -

Analysts said demand to cover short positions in the PGM markets lifted Nymex futures as well as Tocom levels in pre-European trading. Japan's Tocom said earlier on Tuesday it will expand daily limits to make it easier to cover short positions in palladium.
Traders there expect Russia to start shipping August deliveries of PGMs this Thursday.

However, prices remain firm, with palladium touching $246.00 earlier, and platinum reaching $465. The chart target in the latter metal is $500.00, while palladium may well fix at a fresh 17-year high later on Tuesday. Monday's $239.00 fix was just $1 off this recent high.
At 0717 GMT platinum was indicated at $459.00/462.00, while palladium quoted at $240.00/243.00.
GOLD - Action in gold, meanwhile, is seen lacklustre, and there is little sign of the market breaking out of its narrow range.
"We may see slightly lower levels towards $320.00/320.50 by the end of the week, but it does not look too exciting," a European analyst said.
Further ahead, conditions are expected to remain unexciting and there is little chance of the market taking out resistance at $330, he added.
At 0717 GMT spot gold was quoted at $322.80/323.30, down some $0.80 from Monday's close.
SILVER - Silver will probably put on a better show, partly because of the strength of the other white metals, traders said.
"It looks a bit more stable and over the longer-term it could strengthen towards $4.80 or $4.90," the European analyst said.
At 0717 GMT spot silver was quoted at $4.50/4.52, up from the previous close of $4.49/$4.51.
--Martin Hayes, London Newsroom 44 171 542 8080
